## Predicting random effects

Suppose we have the model

$$Y_{ij} = u_i + \varepsilon_{ij}$$

(a single random effect for each group, with no fixed effects). Or, in matrix form:

$$
\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{u} + \boldsymbol{\varepsilon} \hspace{1cm} \boldsymbol{u} \sim N(\boldsymbol{0}, \sigma_u^2\mathbf{I}), \ \ \boldsymbol{\varepsilon} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2 \mathbf{I})
$$

It can be shown that the predicted value for the $i$th group effect $u_i$ is given by

$$\widehat{u}_i = \sigma_u^2 \mathbf{1}^T \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i^{-1} \mathbf{y}_i$$

where $\mathbf{1}$ is the vector of all 1s, $\mathbf{y}_i = (Y_{i1},...,Y_{i n_i})^T$, and 

$$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i^{-1} = \frac{1}{\sigma_{\varepsilon}^4 + n_i \sigma_u^2 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2} \begin{bmatrix} \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2 + (n_i - 1)\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & \cdots & -\sigma_u^2 \\
-\sigma_u^2 & \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2 + (n_i - 1)\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & \cdots & -\sigma_u^2 \\
-\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2 + (n_i - 1)\sigma_u^2  & \cdots & -\sigma_u^2 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
-\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & -\sigma_u^2 & \cdots & \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2 + (n_i - 1)\sigma_u^2\end{bmatrix}$$


## Question

Show that

$$\widehat{u}_i = \frac{1}{n_i + \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2/\sigma_u^2} \sum \limits_{j=1}^{n_i} Y_{ij}$$

How does this compare to the group mean $\dfrac{1}{n_i} \sum \limits_{j=1}^{n_i} Y_{ij}$ ?
